data.title: Middle East Eye: Morning update
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Morning update
Good Morning Middle East Eye readers,
If you are just joining us, here are key developments from across the region and beyond:
*Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says its forces attacked two US bases in Bahrain; Manama says strikes hit civilian industrial facility.
*The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen's Houthis towards Saudi Arabia's western region.
*Two Palestinians injured in an Israeli strike on Gaza succumb as territory's health ministry says death toll since the October 2025 “ceasefire” rises to 1,661.
*Israeli settlers torched Palestinian-owned vehicles and spray-painted alleged racist graffiti on Palestinian homes in several West Bank villages.
*The Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF) has urged Germany to arrest an Israeli soldier, Almog Keisi, who has been sighted in Luneburg this week, accusing him of war crimes, crimes against humanity and acts of genocide in Gaza.
*Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan has said Israel is blocking thousands of container homes destined for Gaza, adding that Israeli authorities argue Hamas could use the metal structures for manufacturing weapons.
*Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that his country was engaged in a "silent war that is far more difficult than the one in which missiles are launched and destruction is inflicted".
*Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has accused Iran of meddling in Lebanon's affairs through Hezbollah's weapons and also demanded Israel withdraw from the country's south.
*Pro-Israel US Democratic leader, Hakeem Jeffries has pledged to advance legislation targeting Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank within the first 100 days of the new Congress.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli settlers torch vehicles in West Bank, paint 'racist' graffiti on homes
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Israeli settlers torch vehicles in West Bank, paint 'racist' graffiti on homes
Israeli settlers set fire to 12 Palestinian-owned vehicles and spray-painted racist graffiti during attacks on three villages in Ramallah and al-Bireh in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian media reported.
Local sources told Wafa that a group of settlers attacked the village of Kafr Malik, east of Ramallah, setting fire to seven vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on the walls of some homes.
In a separate attack, colonists raided the town of Deir Abu Mash'al, northwest of Ramallah, setting fire to three vehicles and spraying racist graffiti before fleeing the area.
In Deir al-Sudan, north of Ramallah, colonists set fire to two vehicles belonging to two Palestinian citizens, causing extensive material damage.
Israeli police, according to Haaretz, said they had opened an investigation into arson, graffiti and property damage at four sites in the West Bank.
Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot condemned the attacks, calling them "Jewish terrorism" and warning that extremist groups setting fire to vehicles and homes were pushing the West Bank toward "anarchy."

data.title: Middle East Eye: How Europe’s green hydrogen ambitions could keep Tunisia’s worst polluter alive
data.author: Francesco Torri
data.summary:
How Europe’s green hydrogen ambitions could keep Tunisia’s worst polluter alive
Submitted by
Francesco Torri
on
Tue, 11/17/2026 - 11:13
A German-backed plan sold as a clean energy transition is seen by many Tunisians as a lifeline for a heavily polluting phosphate industry
Smoke billows from the chimney of a section of the state-run phosphate processing plant in the southern city of Gabes on 31 October 2025 (Fethi Belaid/AFP)
Off
As Tunisia’s green hydrogen strategy is being promoted as a cornerstone of Europe’s clean energy transition, residents in the southern city of Gabes argue it could instead extend the life of one of the country’s most polluting industrial complexes while increasing pressure on scarce resources.
On 21 October 2025, around 100,000 people marched through Gabes in one of the largest environmental protests North Africa has seen in years. Demonstrators demanded the closure of the Groupe Chimique Tunisien (GCT), the state-owned phosphate complex that has polluted the city’s air and sea for decades.
Residents also mobilised against plans to decarbonise the GCT and turn it into a green hydrogen hub supplying Europe. Critics describe the project as a form of “green colonialism”, saying Tunisia would bear the environmental costs while Europe reaps most of the benefits.
Germany, which expects to import 50 to 70 percent of its hydrogen demand by 2030, has been the leading force behind Tunisia’s National Green Hydrogen Strategy, published in July 2024. Berlin financed the strategy and provided the technical expertise behind its design through GIZ’s H2Vert.TUN project.
As the strategy itself states, Tunisia aims to produce 8.3 million tonnes of green hydrogen annually by 2050. Of that total, only around 2 million tonnes would remain in the country. data.title: Middle East Eye: Cop31 ends in failure as countries reject climate deal over fossil fuels
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Cop31 ends in failure as countries reject climate deal over fossil fuels
The United Nations climate summit in Turkey became the longest-ever UN climate conference on Sunday as negotiations over a final agreement descended into deadlock, with the European Union and several other countries formally rejecting the proposed text.
The talks in Antalya, known as Cop31, continued more than 44 hours beyond their scheduled Friday conclusion, surpassing the previous record set by Cop25 in Madrid in 2019.
The latest draft, presented by the Turkish and Australian presidencies in an attempt to bridge divisions between countries, failed to secure consensus over its omission of explicit references to fossil fuels and disagreements over climate finance.
At the closing plenary, Cop31 President Murat Kurum acknowledged that countries had failed to agree on the proposed document.
“We have done our utmost. Ultimately, we have not imposed this text on anyone, nor have we issued an ultimatum such as a ‘take it or leave it’ demand,” Kurum said.
This is a developing story. We'll bring more updates shortly.

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'Jewish terrorism in every sense': Eisenkot blames Smotrich and Ben Gvir for settler attacks
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
'Jewish terrorism in every sense': Eisenkot blames Smotrich and Ben Gvir for settler attacks
Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks by settlers in the occupied West Bank as "Jewish terrorism", accusing far-right ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben Gvir of fuelling violence against Palestinians.
Settlers attacked the villages of Deir al-Sudan, Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik, near Ramallah, overnight between Saturday and Sunday, setting fire to Palestinian-owned vehicles and spraying racist graffiti on homes, according to Palestinian media reports.
Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, described the attacks as "Jewish terrorism in every sense of the word" and called on the government and security establishment to take tougher action against violent settlers.
"The acts of sabotage carried out by extremist groups setting fire to vehicles and homes undermine regional stability, endanger lives and seriously harm Israel's national security and foreign relations," he wrote on X.
Eisenkot was tasked with forming Israel's next government on 8 November by President Isaac Herzog.
He accused National Security Minister Ben Gvir and Finance Minister Smotrich of bringing the West Bank "to the brink of unchecked anarchy".
"This reality is not inevitable," he said, describing it as the consequence of poor leadership.
He said authorities should use all available measures, including administrative detention and targeted operations by the Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency, to stop the perpetrators.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Saudi Arabia, Qatar join condemnation of Iran attack on Bahrain
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Saudi Arabia, Qatar join condemnation of Iran attack on Bahrain
Saudi Arabia and Qatar have joined the UAE in condemning Iran's attack on Bahrain earlier on Sunday.
In a statement posted on X, Qatar's foreign ministry expressed its "categorical rejection of attacks on economic facilities, civilian objects and civilians, and affirms that the continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that threatens the region’s security and stability”.
Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, said it "affirms its full solidarity with Bahrain in all measures it takes to protect its security and stability", accusing Tehran of "undermining regional security and stability”.
Iran attacked US military bases in both Qatar and Saudi Arabia, along with Bahrain, Kuwait, the UAE, Oman, Iraq and Jordan throughout the first months of the war, which began in late February. But such attacks have lulled since April amid ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

data.author: Daniel Tester

Israel: Eisenkot and Netanyahu parties meet again for unity government talks
Representatives from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and the party of his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar, met on Sunday to discuss forming a unity government, Haaretz is reporting.
The meeting follows earlier talks last Sunday after nearly a month of deadlock in the Israeli Knesset since October's election, which saw no party gain an overall majority. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have so far failed to negotiate a viable coalition government alongside smaller parties.
Absent from Sunday's meeting were representatives of Naftali Bennett's Together party, which received the third-largest vote share and attended the previous round of talks.

data.title: Middle East Eye: 'Deserved to fail': Cop31 ends in failure as countries reject deal over fossil fuels
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:

Submitted by
MEE staff
on

European Union, Panama and other countries reject the final proposal over its failure to explicitly address fossil fuels
Cop31 President and Turkey's Minister of Environment Murat Kurum attends a session of the UN Climate Change Conference (Cop31) in Antalya on 22 November 2026 (AFP)
Off
The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey ended without agreement after the European Union and several countries rejected a proposed deal that failed to explicitly address fossil fuels and provide stronger financial support to developing nations.
Cop31 President Murat Kurum said that the negotiations had failed to secure consensus, adding that the proposed decisions had not been adopted.
"It is clear that there are parties in this hall who oppose this text. We recognise that there is no consensus on this document. Therefore, these decisions have not been adopted," he told the closing plenary.
"We have done our utmost. Ultimately, we have not imposed this text on anyone, nor have we issued an ultimatum such as a 'take it or leave it' demand."
The European Union, the Marshall Islands, Panama, Norway and Vanuatu were among those that formally objected to the proposed Antalya Pact.
The talks had been scheduled to end on Friday but continued until Sunday, as negotiators tried to resolve disagreements over the proposed agreement.
The breakdown followed more than two weeks of negotiations, making the summit the longest in the history of the UN climate conference process.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
Iran's navy said on Sunday that two supertankers hit naval mines and caught fire after entering a "restricted area" east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported.
According to the Fars news agency, the navy said the tankers had switched off their detection and navigation systems and struck the mines north of Ghanam Island.
Both vessels reportedly stopped moving.
Supertankers usually carry two million barrels of oil or more, about twice as much as a standard tanker.
The navy also warned that relying on "smugglers such as CENTCOM", referring to US Central Command, would result in "nothing but heavy losses".
UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) also said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman.
It gave no further details, saying only that authorities were aware and an investigation was under way. It was unclear whether the incident involved either of the tankers Iran described.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
Bahrain said on Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on “a civilian industrial site” in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed earlier in November.
"In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain… a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded," Bahrain's interior ministry said on X.
"His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition."
Residents had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco, AFP reported.
In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the IRGC said they had attacked US Patriot air defence systems with missiles and drones at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic.
Bahrain's foreign ministry dismissed the IRGC's account, saying the site hit was purely civilian and industrial, calling the attack a direct danger to civilians and a violation of the kingdom's sovereignty.
Bahrain's neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday also condemned Tehran for its attacks on Gulf countries.
The Saudi foreign ministry expressed on X "the strongest condemnation and denunciation... of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain".
As a result of the heinous Iranian attacks on Bahrain yesterday, a Bahraini citizen with disabilities sustained injuries and is in stable condition, while a Pakistani resident was also injured and is in critical condition. Both are receiving treatment in the hospital. #Bahrain #MOI

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher, as senior military commanders touted the Islamic Republic's capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.
"A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time," Iranian state television reported on Saturday.
State television broadcast footage of Ahmad Vahidi, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC's Aerospace Force, touring an underground missile base.
The two commanders were shown riding on top of a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment.
"The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation," Vahidi said.
"Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy," said Mousavi.
During the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes targeted the country's missile capabilities and hit its nuclear sites for a second time, though the extent of the damage remains unclear.
Earlier this month, the IRGC unveiled what it described as new underground "missile cities" housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Two Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in northern and central Gaza
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Two Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in northern and central Gaza
Israeli forces killed two Palestinians in separate attacks in the Gaza Strip on Sunday, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.
One was shot dead by Israeli gunfire in Jabalia, north of Gaza, on Sunday evening.
Earlier in the evening, an Israeli quadcopter drone struck and killed another Palestinian in eastern Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza.
Israel has killed more than 1,600 Palestinians in Gaza since the ceasefire agreement of October 2025.
At least 74,742 Palestinians have been killed and 176,227 wounded since the war began in October 2023.
